At step n (for n = 1, 2, 3, ...), you add ten new balls numbered 10n−9 through 10n into a vase, then remove the single ball numbered n. All infinitely many steps happen within one minute (each step taking half as long as the one before it). At the exact end of the minute, how many balls are left in the vase?
choices: Infinitely many, since ten balls go in for every one that comes out
0 — every ball, however large its number, is eventually removed at its own numbered step, so none remain unremoved
It's undefined — the process has no well-defined outcome
Exactly 1, the very last ball added

questions.q: In a study, people who scored in the bottom quartile on a test of logical reasoning rated their own ability as well above average, while the top performers slightly underestimated how they ranked against peers. What is this effect called, where people with low ability at a task tend to overestimate their competence, partly because the same skills needed to perform well are also needed to judge performance accurately?

A ship has every one of its wooden planks replaced over the years, one by one, until literally none of the original material remains. Philosophers ask whether the fully-replaced ship is still 'the same ship' it always was. What is the name of this classic identity paradox?

Two players, A and B, are playing a game to 10 points: each round is decided by an independent fair coin flip, awarding one point to the winner. They must stop early when A has 8 points and B has 7. To split the prize fairly — in proportion to each player's probability of winning had the game continued — what ratio of the pot should A and B receive?
choices: 1:1, since the game never actually finished
